title: Managed Service Privacy & Security Appendix (vendor template)
body:
Purpose and intended use:

This document is a template appendix intended to be attached to a Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Statement of Work (SOW) when Redwood Inference engages a third-party managed-service vendor that will process, store, or otherwise have access to Customer Data or Redwood Confidential Information. It is designed to be vendor-facing but also to capture minimum security and privacy commitments required by Redwood. Legal may redline for jurisdictional or customer-specific requirements. Security should review and sign off prior to vendor negotiations.

How to use this template:
- Replace placeholders in double-braces (e.g., {{VendorName}}, {{EffectiveDate}}).
- Sections marked "Negotiation Guidance" provide internal notes and fallback language.
- Attach vendor attestation and evidence (SOC2/ISO certs, penetration test reports) in Appendix A.

1. Definitions (selected)
- "Redwood Data": any data provided by Redwood, Redwood customers, or generated by the services in connection with the Agreement, including Personal Data as defined below.
- "Personal Data": information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, as defined under applicable data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).
- "Processing": any operation performed on Redwood Data, whether or not by automated means.
- "Subprocessor": any third party engaged by Vendor to process Redwood Data.

2. Scope and Purpose
2.1 Appendix scope: This Appendix governs the Processing of Redwood Data by Vendor in connection with the services described in the Agreement.
2.2 Purpose limitation: Vendor shall only Process Redwood Data for the purposes set out in the Agreement and as documented in Exhibit 1 (Permitted Purposes). Any additional Processing requires prior written authorization from Redwood.

3. Data Categories and Data Subjects
3.1 Categories of Data: Vendor may process the following categories of data: service telemetry, application logs, configuration metadata, developer names and contact info, and customer-submitted text or files that may include Personal Data.
3.2 Data Subjects: Redwood employees, contractors, customers, and end users.

4. Roles and Controller/Processor Allocations
- Redwood: Controller for Customer Data (unless otherwise agreed).
- Vendor: Processor. Where Vendor acts as Controller for any subset of data, that must be described and expressly agreed.

5. Data Transfers and Cross-Border Processing
5.1 Geographic restrictions: Vendor shall not transfer Redwood Data outside the countries listed in Exhibit 2 without Redwood's prior written consent.
5.2 Transfer mechanisms: For transfers from the EEA/UK, Vendor must rely on an approved transfer mechanism (e.g., EU SCCs, UK Addendum, binding corporate rules). Vendor will provide executed SCCs on request.

Negotiation Guidance: Prefer list of allowed regions rather than open-ended global transfer language. Require subprocessors outside approved regions to have compensating controls and prior notification.

6. Security Measures (minimum requirements)
Vendor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect Redwood Data, including but not limited to:
- Access controls: Role-based access, least privilege, MFA for administrative accounts, regular access review (at least quarterly).
- Encryption: Data at rest encrypted with industry standard algorithms (AES-256 or equivalent); data in transit using TLS 1.2+; KMS controls for key management and separation where keys are customer-specific or designated by Redwood.
- Network security: Dedicated VPCs or logically isolated tenants, egress controls, firewall rules, and segmentation between production and non-production environments.
- Vulnerability management: Regular vulnerability scanning, prioritized patching for critical/high findings within 30 days, and documented processes for emergency patching.
- Secure development: Secure SDLC practices, code review for privileged changes, dependency scanning and remediation for critical CVEs.
- Logging and monitoring: Retain security and access logs for at least 90 days (longer if required by Exhibit 3), centralized logging, and dashboards for anomalous activity.
- Data lifecycle controls: Procedures for ingestion, classification, retention, archival, and secure deletion of Redwood Data.
- Incident response: Formal IR plan, incident manager, runbooks for data breaches, notification timelines (see Section 8).

Negotiation Guidance: Where Vendor cannot meet a specific control, require compensating controls and timeline to remediate. For high-risk services consider contractual right to require specific cloud configuration or dedicated instances.

7. Subprocessors
7.1 Authorization: Vendor may engage Subprocessors only with prior general written authorization (e.g., the types listed in Exhibit 4) and after providing written notice of any new Subprocessor at least 30 days before onboarding.
7.2 Contractual flowdown: Vendor must flow down equivalent data protection obligations to Subprocessors by contract.
7.3 Subprocessor auditability: Upon reasonable notice, Redwood or an independent auditor may assess Subprocessor compliance via audit, questionnaire, or by reviewing attestations (SOC2, ISO 27001).

Negotiation Guidance: Push for a right to object to Subprocessors and to require removal of a Subprocessor where redlines fail.

8. Security Incidents and Breach Notification
8.1 Notification timing: Vendor shall notify Redwood of any confirmed or suspected security incident affecting Redwood Data within 24 hours of detection (initial notice) and provide a substantive update within 72 hours.
8.2 Contents of notice: description of incident, scope of impact, categories of data affected, remedial actions taken, and contact details for the incident response lead.
8.3 Cooperation and remediation: Vendor shall cooperate with Redwood (and regulators where applicable), provide forensic evidence, and remediate the cause of the incident at Vendor's expense if due to Vendor negligence.

Negotiation Guidance: For high-sensitivity data, consider shorter initial notification windows (e.g., 12 hours) and a dedicated incident response communication channel.

9. Audit Rights and Assessments
9.1 Audit methods: Redwood may conduct audits via: (a) review of Vendor's certifications and third-party reports (SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001), (b) security questionnaires (e.g., SIG, CAIQ), and (c) on-site audits with reasonable notice.
9.2 Frequency and scope: Annual review standard; more frequent audits permitted if a material incident occurs or regulatory obligations require it.

Negotiation Guidance: If Vendor refuses on-site audits, accept attestations plus right to a targeted remote assessment or a third-party assessor.

10. Security Testing and Penetration Tests
- Vendor shall conduct annual external penetration tests and internal network assessments and provide summary findings and remediation timelines to Redwood.
- Redwood may request targeted tests against Vendor systems that process Redwood Data, subject to written rules of engagement and mutual agreement on timing to avoid service disruption.

11. Data Retention, Deletion, and Return
11.1 Retention: Vendor will retain Redwood Data only for as long as necessary to provide the services or as required by law.
11.2 Deletion/Return: Upon expiration or termination, Vendor shall, at Redwood's option, return all Redwood Data within 30 days in a mutually agreed format or securely destroy it and certify destruction.
11.3 Residual copies: Vendor may retain residual backups for a limited period for disaster recovery; residual copies must be encrypted and destroyed within 90 days unless otherwise agreed.

12. Confidentiality and Personnel
- Confidentiality obligations that survive termination for a minimum of 5 years.
- Personnel with access to Redwood Data must be subject to confidentiality agreements, background checks where required, and least-privilege access.

13. Liability, Indemnities, and Insurance
- Vendor indemnifies Redwood for breaches caused by Vendor's negligence or willful misconduct.
- Minimum cyber insurance requirements: $5M per incident (adjustable based on risk).
- Cap on liability: Negotiation item — Redwood prefers carve-outs for data protection liabilities and breaches of confidentiality.

14. Regulatory Compliance and Cooperation
- Vendor will comply with applicable privacy and security laws (GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA, etc.) and regulatory requests affecting Redwood Data.
- Vendor will assist Redwood with data subject requests (access, deletion, portability) as required by applicable law and within agreed SLAs (e.g., 10 business days for initial response).

15. Change Control and Security Roadmap
- Vendor will provide Redwood at least 60 days' notice of changes to technical architecture, key Subprocessors, or security posture that materially affect Redwood Data processing.
- Vendor to provide annual security roadmap and remediation plan for open findings.

16. Remedies and Termination
- Redwood may suspend data flows or terminate the Agreement for material security breaches or failure to remediate critical findings within agreed timelines.
- Equitable remedies: Redwood may seek injunctive relief to stop unauthorized processing.

17. Appendices (required attachments)
- Exhibit 1: Permitted Purposes and Processing Activities (detailed table).
- Exhibit 2: Approved Processing Regions and Transfer Mechanisms.
- Exhibit 3: Log Retention, Monitoring, and SIEM Integration Requirements.
- Exhibit 4: Current Subprocessors (table).
- Appendix A: Attestations and Evidence (SOC2 report, ISO certs, pentest summaries).

18. Internal Checklist (Security & Legal pre-sign)
- Confirm scope aligns with SOW.
- Confirm data categories and any high-risk data (health, financial, government).
- Request and validate SOC2 Type II or ISO 27001 certification and review last 12 months of remediation items.
- Verify encryption and key management approach.
- Validate geographic restrictions and transfer mechanisms.
- Confirm breach notification SLAs and escalation matrix.
- Agree insurance and liability carve-outs.

Negotiation Guidance (summary):
- Push to limit Subprocessor locations and require prior notice for new Subprocessors.
- Insist on transparent evidence (SOC2/ISO) and right to targeted assessments.
- Require short incident notification windows and substantive updates.
- Keep retention and deletion windows explicit.

Redlines & suggested alternative language (examples)
- If Vendor resists 24-hour notification: propose 24-hour initial notification with 72-hour substantive update; if Vendor still resists, accept 48-hour initial notice with commitment to expedite critical incidents.
- If Vendor resists full contract flowdown to Subprocessors: require flowdown for all material obligations (security, breach notification, deletion).
